Hub-Spectral Activation of Latent Multimodal Knowledge

A shared hub can hide useful cross-modal relations that native similarity scores do not reliably expose.

Guo Ying·Chen Haidong·Xu Linrui·Liu Xiaohao·Shi Chuancheng·Xiao Canran·Zhang Dan·Shen Fei·Shen Li·Chua Tat-Seng

September 15, 2026 ·Preprint ·Read the paper ·PDF ·Code
1Why this matters 2How it works 3What the study finds 4What this means

The short version

HSA recovers and activates the hub-readable part of latent multimodal knowledge from frozen representations using closed-form statistical and spectral operations.

31.15%Mean bidirectional Recall@10
52.43%Mean macro Top-1 accuracy
19 + 11Retrieval + classification relations

Why this matters

Training two modalities against a shared hub does not guarantee their mutual alignment. The question is which part of their relation is identifiable from the two trained hub edges.

How it works

  1. Compose and standardize the second-order statistics of the two source-trained hub edges.
  2. Extract paired spectral directions to represent the hub-readable component.
  3. Combine reliability-weighted matching and source-gated candidate resolution for retrieval and prototype classification.

What the study finds

Across ImageBind and LanguageBind, mean bidirectional Recall@10 rises from 18.27% to 31.15% over 19 relations. Mean macro Top-1 rises from 29.01% to 52.43% over 11 prototype-classification relations.

What this means

The result concerns a source-induced, hub-readable component under the stated statistical model. It shows why a frozen representation can contain useful relations beyond its native similarity interface.
